old_exception.reason: Spec 8.3's Noto Emoji substitution. U+1F600 and U+1F389 are absent from every official font chunk, so revision 1 shapes each from the complete monochrome Noto Emoji 3.003 face and reports one font.noto-emoji-substituted per affected occurrence (decided on #121). The official export has no bundled glyph for them either: its font list ends in the local-only Segoe UI Emoji, which the pinned container's fontconfig resolves to Noto Color Emoji 2.047, so the browser draws colour bitmap glyphs. The divergence is the emoji cells on both lines, colour bitmaps against monochrome outlines at near-identical advances, plus the trailing Latin word each cell shifts by at most three pixels. The leading Latin word on both lines differs only by the sub-pixel glyph-coverage class recorded on #104, #105, #108 and #110. With #169 the renderer snaps each line's baseline to the device pixel grid as the canvas does, so what remains is the two rasterizers' coverage of identically placed outlines.

old_exception.reason: Spec 8.3's replacement glyph. No bundled face maps a Hebrew or Arabic scalar, so revision 1 shapes each as the deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans and reports it as font.missing-glyph, and shapes the trailing paragraph separator U+2029 the same way (decided on #124 and #125). The official export has no bundled glyph for them either and falls through to the pinned container's system fonts: FreeSans for Hebrew in Excalifont text and the system Liberation Sans for Hebrew in Helvetica text, FreeSerif for Arabic in both, and FreeSans's blank advance for the separator. The divergence is each right-to-left cell against its ? glyphs and, on the same line, the Latin word or punctuation the differing advances displace toward the line's unanchored side; the anchored side agrees pixel for pixel (the leading words of the left-aligned lines, the trailing words of the right-aligned lines, the centres of the centred lines), so the visual run order, the digits placed before the Arabic run, the exclamation mark after the Hebrew run and the mirrored bracket pair, matches the official export. The Latin words differ only by the sub-pixel glyph-coverage class recorded on #104, #105, #108, #110, #153 and #169. With #169 the renderer snaps each line's baseline to the device pixel grid as the canvas does; what remains is the two rasterizers' coverage of identically placed outlines and, for the Helvetica-family lines, the reference profile's light autohinting of the container's system Liberation Sans, whose x-height it snaps to the pixel grid (spec 8.5).
